gate_claims.claim: the testbench is the file that declares the run's top module
only the testbench may end the simulation, read arguments or open a file; another file that does is refused before anything runs
the simulation job is refused when a design file uses a testbench-only construct, with nothing simulated
the testbench-only constructs are the listed system tasks, plusargs, file opening, system calls and DPI
the testbench must print one verdict line NIRMAAN-SIM <nonce> <n> passed, <m> failed
the run fails when the verdict is missing
the run fails when the verdict is repeated
the run fails when the verdict reports a failed check
the run fails when the verdict reports no passed check
a verdict line without this run's nonce is not counted (forged)
the must-fail scorer: the clean RTL must pass and each planted mutant must fail the same testbench
each mutant must fail on a run that executed; a refused run is not a mutant caught
a scoreboard written in Python for cocotb has the same limit: cocotb counts tests, so a test with no assertion passes
cocotb requires at least one passing test
the sentence that a passing run does not say the model is right: the gate has no view of the model (no check on the model exists in the parser)
